title: Add flake score, automatic rerun policy, and aggregation for Optimize quality gates
author: Olivia Grant
description: Context: Optimize quality gates run offline eval suites to decide whether a proposed batching/caching/quantization config diff is safe to apply. In beta we’ve been seeing occasional noisy regressions driven by nondeterminism (model sampling variance, evaluator jitter, infra blips) and prompt-set sensitivity. This PR introduces (1) a formal flakiness score computed per suite/run, (2) an automatic rerun policy with bounded cost and clear exit conditions, and (3) deterministic aggregation of multiple attempts into a single GateRunResult that downstream services can consume. Key behaviors: - Each gate run attempt produces AttemptResult (raw metrics, rubric outputs, infra metadata, error codes). - Flake score (0.0–1.0) is computed from cross-attempt dispersion on primary metrics + attempt-level failure signals (timeouts, evaluator exceptions), normalized by metric type and minimum sample size. - Rerun policy triggers up to max_attempts (default 3) when results are inconclusive (near-threshold deltas) or high flake score; policy does not rerun when a clear regression is detected beyond the hard-fail margin. - Aggregation uses median-of-attempts for scalar metrics and majority vote for boolean success metrics; confidence bounds are derived from attempt dispersion and sample size, and included in the response. - API response gains: flake_score, attempts, rerun_reason (if any), aggregated_confidence, and a stable decision field: passed | failed | inconclusive. Inconclusive is explicitly treated as fail-by-default for enforcement, but allows a targeted override workflow upstream. This change is backwards compatible: existing callers that only read decision + deltas continue to work; new fields are additive. Follow-ups: wiring quarantine tooling and surfacing flake signals in dashboards is tracked in ENG-3926/ENG-3929; Optimize service integration is tracked in ENG-3922.

implementation_notes: Flake score details: For each primary metric m, compute delta-to-baseline per attempt. Let MAD be median absolute deviation across attempts (robust to outliers). Normalize dispersion by an expected-variance term derived from sample size (n) and metric type. Add penalty terms for attempt errors (timeout, evaluator error) and high retry rate. Final flake_score = clamp01(w_dispersion * norm_dispersion + w_error * error_rate + w_near * near_threshold_rate). Defaults (configurable per suite): w_dispersion=0.65, w_error=0.25, w_near=0.10; near-threshold window defaults to 0.5x the regression threshold. Rerun policy details: attempt 1 always runs; attempt 2 runs if (flake_score >= 0.35) OR (abs(delta) within near-threshold window) OR transient error code; attempt 3 runs if after 2 attempts decision is inconclusive OR flake_score >= 0.55, bounded by max_attempts. Early exit occurs if hard-fail is exceeded (delta worse than threshold + margin) or hard-pass is exceeded (delta better than -margin) with low flake score. Aggregation details: scalar metrics use median; confidence is reported as an interval derived from MAD (scaled) + sample size floor; boolean success uses majority vote with tie -> inconclusive; any attempt marked non-transient infra failure increments error penalties but does not automatically fail unless all attempts fail. All attempts and their artifact pointers are included in the response for audit/debug.
conversation: Sana Farid (review): How are we normalizing dispersion across different metric scales? Also, we should avoid treating “near threshold” as synonymous with “flaky” unless we can separate signal vs noise. Olivia Grant (author): Added per-metric normalization (expected variance term) and split near-threshold penalty to a small independent weight. Flake score primarily comes from cross-attempt dispersion and error rate; near-threshold only influences rerun triggers and contributes 0.10 by default. Jonas Weber (review): Please ensure we don’t rerun when it’s clearly failed; cost will blow up on big suites. Also want the decision to be stable for Optimize enforcement. Olivia Grant (author): Implemented hard-fail early exit (threshold + margin) and hard-pass early exit; decision field is now passed/failed/inconclusive and aggregation is deterministic via median/majority. Selene Huang (review): Inconclusive must be explicit and visible; do not collapse into failed silently. Also add artifacts for each attempt so we can debug evaluator drift. Olivia Grant (author): Done. API response includes attempts[] with artifact URIs and rerun_reason. Connor O'Brien (review): CI: add a contract test to ensure additive schema change won’t break callers; also ensure migrations are safe for rollbacks. Olivia Grant (author): Added schema test and made persistence change additive (nullable attempts field). Migration is backward compatible; rollback keeps reading the old fields. Allison Grant (review): Please add structured logs/tags for rerun cause and flake_score so dashboards can break down by suite and region. Olivia Grant (author): Added log keys: gate_run_id, suite_id, flake_score, rerun_reason, attempt_idx, error_code; also propagates region and runner_pool labels.
